items: Customer surveys gather information from many customers online, by phone or in person; before opening a bakery, ask neighbours which baked goods they want, when they buy and how much they spend.
Focus groups bring a small, diverse group together to discuss a product in depth; participants taste breads and pastries and discuss likes, dislikes and improvements.

blocks.prompt: When would a focus group be better than a survey?
blocks.explanation: When you need to understand why people feel as they do, for example their detailed reactions to tasting a new product, rather than counting answers.

items: Surveys: many people, structured questions. Focus groups: a few people, deep discussion.
